newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Dealers try to gauge crop damage.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Dealers try to gauge crop damage.

text.p: Grain merchandisers in the U.S. High Plains said Monday they were trying to gauge how much of the U.S. hard red winter wheat crop would be lost after damage from unseasonably cold weekend weather.
Dealers said that although signs pointed to severe damage in Kansas, Oklahoma and Texas, the extent of damage will probably not be known until warmer temperatures return later this week.
"It's very, very difficult to assess right now," one dealer in south central Kansas said. "We haven't had enough sun or heat on this to know anything yet."
One dealer said that everything to the north of Salina, Kan., was probably undamaged.
"From Salina north there's no damage because we had snow cover and the crop just wasn't all that developed," the dealer said.

Meanwhile, basis levels were unchanged to mostly lower in line with the run-up in futures prices Friday and expected further sharp gains at the Kansas City Board of Trade Monday, linked to the cold weather.
Movement was nil as growers waited to see how high prices will climb before they decide to sell, dealers said.
